evidence.reason: At the pinned code, boot() calls subprocess.Popen at lines 712-713 and then recorder.append at 714-715 outside the try/except that begins at line 716. If the recorder write raises, execution bypasses the cleanup at lines 730-753 that stops the scope and terminates/reaps the child. The spawned systemd-run/QEMU process can therefore survive after boot() unwinds and the caller releases the run lock, with no process.json identity for cleanup. This is an exception-safety defect in the existing cleanup behavior, not a new requirement; the minimal fix is to put the recorder write inside the guarded block or otherwise run the existing terminate/wait cleanup before re-raising.
